correctness.summary: The beta-gamma factorization reduces the equal-weight perturbation to a smooth scalar scale mixture. Its second and fourth beta moments give the stated quadratic and critical quartic coefficients by implicit quantile expansion. Conditioning at the two endpoints gives the first derivatives, and the source distributional representations yield the variance-gamma and McKay rates. Direct numerical inversion of exact one-dimensional cdf representations supports all displayed coefficients.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Gaunt and Ouimet (2026) prove global median monotonicity and endpoint limits but do not state the general-q local curvature, critical quartic refinement, or endpoint rates claimed here. Classical Bock et al., Diaconis-Perlman, and Yu results cover majorization and crossing phenomena and are not claimed. Searches found no equivalent explicit formulas. The full Bock et al. (1987) and Diaconis-Perlman (1990) texts were not directly inspected, leaving residual risk for the weighted-gamma component.

value.summary: The formulas identify an exact quantile phase transition in the local effect of weight imbalance, resolve the degenerate transition at fourth order, and sharpen qualitative variance-gamma and McKay median endpoint limits into explicit convergence rates.

limitations: Local parameter expansions; no new global quantile crossing theorem.
No uniform remainder bounds over q, r, or family parameters.
The complete Diaconis-Perlman (1990) and Bock et al. (1987) texts were not directly inspected.
Independent audit has not been performed.
